source.name: CDC Learn the Signs. Act Early.
source.note: months = CDC checkpoint: age by which most babies (about 75%) do this. Stage texts and optional steps are editorial.

steps.text: Smiles when you talk to or smile at them
Smiles on their own to get your attention
Chuckles when you try to make them laugh
Laughs
Smiles or laughs at peek-a-boo
Calms down when spoken to or picked up
Looks at your face
Seems happy to see you walk up
Looks, moves or makes sounds to get or keep your attention
Knows familiar people
Is shy, clingy or fearful around strangers
Reacts when you leave (looks, reaches for you or cries)
Likes to look at self in a mirror
Shows several facial expressions: happy, sad, angry, surprised
Plays games with you, like pat-a-cake
Makes sounds other than crying
Coos: "oooo", "aahh"
Makes sounds back when you talk
Takes turns making sounds with you
Blows raspberries
Makes squealing noises
Makes many different sounds: "mamamama", "babababa"
Calls a parent "mama", "dada" or another special name
Reacts to loud sounds
Turns head towards your voice
Looks when you call their name
Understands "no" (pauses or stops)
Lifts arms up to be picked up
Waves bye-bye
Watches you as you move
Looks at a toy for several seconds
Looks at their hands with interest
Puts things in mouth to explore them
Reaches to grab a toy they want
Bangs two things together
Puts something in a container, like a block in a cup
Looks for objects dropped out of sight
Looks for things they see you hide
If hungry, opens mouth at the breast or bottle
Closes lips to show they don't want more
Holds head up when on tummy
Pushes up onto elbows or forearms on tummy
Holds head steady without support when held
Pushes up with straight arms on tummy
Moves both arms and both legs
Opens hands briefly
Brings hands to mouth
Holds a toy put in their hand
Swings arm at toys
Moves things from one hand to the other
Uses fingers to rake food towards self
Picks things up between thumb and pointer finger
Drinks from a cup without a lid, as you hold it
Rolls from tummy to back
Leans on hands for support when sitting
Sits without support
Gets to a sitting position alone
Crawls (optional: not all babies crawl)
Pulls up to stand
Walks holding on to furniture

stages.title: Initial install
stages.summary: The system boots up: learning faces and voices, eating, sleeping and rebooting several times a day.
normal: "Crib not accepted" mode: may wake when put down in the crib.
Low battery with no warning: gets fussy after being awake a long time.
Asks to feed more often on some days.
ideas: Talk face to face when they're awake and calm.
A little tummy time, awake and always supervised.
Answer their sounds, as if you were chatting.
stages.next: First responsive smiles may be on the way.

stages.title: Smile update
stages.summary: More interaction: smiles on purpose, cooing and a big interest in their own hands.
normal: Serious face mode: may just watch everything with deep focus.
Hands are the favorite new feature and go straight to the mouth.
Nap times still change from day to day.
ideas: Take turns talking: you speak, wait, and let them answer their way.
Awake tummy time with toys in view.
Offer a toy for them to hold.
stages.next: Laughs and grabbing everything may be coming.

stages.title: Hands & laughs update
stages.summary: Grabs, tastes, laughs and starts to know their people.
normal: Everything goes through mouth quality control (watch out for small objects).
ideas: Put safe toys within reach so they go after them.
Play in front of a mirror.
Repeat their sounds and let them answer.

stages.title: Mobility update
stages.summary: Sits, babbles eagerly and starts noticing who is around and who isn't.
normal: New "stranger shyness" feature: may only want their own people.
Drops things to see if they come back. System testing.
May protest when you leave the room.
ideas: Name what they see and what they do.
Baby-proof: outlets, stairs and small objects.
stages.next: Standing, gestures and a special word may be coming.

stages.title: Almost-one release
stages.summary: Stands up, waves bye-bye and understands more than it seems.
normal: Understands "no" and sometimes tests it anyway.
Finds the tiniest crumb on the floor.
ideas: Hide a toy under a blanket for them to find.
Give them blocks and a cup to fill and empty.
stages.next: First steps and more words usually come after the first year, each at their own pace.

notice: This is a guide, not a test or a deadline: every baby has their own pace. If something worries you, if they lose skills they had, or if you have questions, talk to your pediatrician. Under 3 months, a fever of 38 °C (100.4 °F) or higher needs medical care right away.
